# dsh-codex-effort-switcher
English | 中文
## Summary
Replaces the composer's model picker with a Codex-style card: the effort label, an opaque segmented
effort slider, and the provider-grouped model list. Install the packed archive into a profile and re
start; removing the package restores the shipped picker with no residue. The `/model` command, the s
ettings Models page, and the Host selection path stay as shipped, so a switch made in either place i
s what the other shows next. The card is a second occupant of the composer's single-occupant model s
lot at `priority: -1`, reading the same per-session `modelDirectories` service, and it provides the
`codexModelTiers` client service for plugins that append a tier.
## Install
Build the package inside this directory; development dependencies and artifacts remain here. Use a N
ode.js version supported by DSH.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Alternatively install the absolute `.tgz` path from DSH's plugin manager. Install into the profile y
ou use, and use Desktop's own plugin manager for Desktop: the CLI refuses a profile the application
manages. Restart the app afterwards, because a profile without live patch reloading composes the new
bundle at boot. This plugin does not install itself into any profile.
## Use
Click the model chip at the right of the composer. The card opens on the effort face: the current le
vel (blue, with a chevron) above the model name, over one dot per advertised level. Both lines are a
single button, and clicking anywhere on it opens the model list. The flat channel carries a solid p
ill whose edge tracks the knob; the outer stops keep clear of its rounded ends, and the top tier fil
ls exactly that range. Click a dot, or scrub the track horizontally; the circular arrow restores the
model's default level. At the model's highest level the pill turns from blue to violet and light-vi
olet motes drift across it from right to left. The 选择模型 face lists each provider group, with a check
on the current model. Selecting a model keeps the current level on the same route and takes the tar
get route's default level otherwise.
The panel stays open while you change anything in it — a level, the model, or the default — so sever
al levels can be compared without reopening it. An outside click dismisses it; Escape leaves the 选择模
型 face for the effort face first, then dismisses the panel.
The trigger shows the model name and the level and keeps its shipped accessible name; the composer's
compact mode still collapses it to the model glyph. `Esc` leaves a drilled face before closing the
card; arrow keys move focus; a rejected selection reports through the app toast, and a catalog that
fails to load offers Retry inside the card.
## How it composes with DSH
The composer model seat is a single-occupant slot. This plugin registers a second occupant at `prior
ity: -1`, which shadows the shipped picker without unloading it, and reads the same per-session `mod
elDirectories` service — so a switch made in either this card or `/model` is what the other shows ne
xt, and the Host still receives one `session.selectModel` call. Removing the plugin restores the shi
pped picker with no residue.
Provider headings appear only when more than one provider has models; a single-provider catalog rend
ers a flat list. The card is opaque by design: it uses the theme's selector surface rather than the
translucent menu material. There is no search field; the list scrolls.
Uninstalling removes the bundle layer and the card; saved model selections and the session log are u
ing removes the bundle layer and the card; saved model selections and the session log are untouched.
## Third-party tiers
The browser half provides the `codexModelTiers` client service (`SeatTierRegistry`). A client plugin
can add an effort tier above the model's own levels by injecting the service and registering a `Sea
tTier` with `id`, `label`, `description`, `available(model)`, `effort(model)`, `active(sessionId)`,
and `apply(sessionId, selection, model, select)`. The card appends registered tiers after the shippe
d efforts; `apply` receives the standard `select` function, so the Host still sees exactly one `sess
ion.selectModel`. The top tier gets the violet `data-ultra` skin. Without a contributor the registry
is empty and the card is unchanged; removing a contributor removes its tier without touching select
ions or the session log.
A tier contributor is an ordinary client plugin: it injects the service, registers its tier, and may
ship its own Host half for whatever the tier means beyond the effort. The dependency runs one way —
the contributor depends on this package, never the reverse.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The first two commands run independently; the switcher test also covers a contributed tier. The brow
ser smoke packs the plugin, installs it into a throwaway `DSH_HOME` profile through `apps/cli/lib/bi
n.js`, points a fixture provider at a local model endpoint, boots `dsh web` from the DSH checkout, a
nd drives Microsoft Edge through the real card — asserting the faces, the slider, viewport fitting,
the routed model, and the routed reasoning-effort wire value. It needs `pnpm run build` in the DSH c
heckout and writes ignored evidence under `.runtime/`. Published packages exclude tests and developm
s ignored evidence under `.runtime/`. Published packages exclude tests and development dependencies.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- The model slot is single-occupant, so two plugins shadowing it at the same priority throw.
- The c

ard is opaque by design and carries no search field.
- Provider headings appear only when more than

one provider has models.
- A contributed tier renders above the shipped efforts, and two tiers shari

ng an `id` throw.
- Desktop installs go through the desktop application's own plugin manager; the CL

I refuses a profile the application manages.
- The bundle is composed at boot, so a profile without
live patch reloading needs an application restart.
